title: Special Education and Counseling
tagline: Every learner deserves a counselor who understands.
welcome: Children with disabilities and learning differences need counselors who understand both their minds and their systems. This course prepares you.
vignette: A nonverbal autistic ten-year-old is labeled 'non-compliant' for leaving circle time. The counselor watches and sees overwhelm, not defiance, and proposes a quiet corner and a visual schedule. Understanding changes the story, and the child's day.
vignette_attr: An inclusion classroom moment, drawn from practice
description: A course at the intersection of special education and counseling: categories and lived experience of disability, the IEP process and the counselor's role, counseling adaptations for diverse learners, collaboration with special educators and families, and advocacy and inclusion.
questions: How do I counsel a child whose communication differs from mine?
What is my role on the IEP team?
How do I advocate for inclusion without ignoring real needs?
importance: Children with disabilities face elevated mental-health risk
Counselors are mandated members of the educational team
Adapted counseling makes support real for diverse learners
misconceptions: that disability defines the child, when it is one facet of a whole person
that counseling must be standard to be effective, when adaptation is effectiveness
figures: whose multiple intelligences widened the view of ability
whose ecology frames the child in systems
who insisted on belonging as a right
outcomes: You will know major disabilities and the child's perspective.
You will contribute as a counselor on the team.
You will modify communication and techniques for diverse learners.
You will work as a partner in the child's plan.
You will foster belonging and peer understanding.
You will champion dignity and appropriate support.
modules: The child's and family's lived experience
The IEP Process and the Counselor
The IEP is where systems meet the child.
Adaptation is clinical skill, not compromise.
The child's team must pull together.
Inclusion is built peer by peer.
Advocacy is counseling at the system level.
assessment: Assessment is team and adaptation focused.
tips: Presume competence and seek the child's channel
Learn the child's communication system first
Bring the child's voice into every meeting
integration: Special-education competence completes your school and clinical preparation.
faith: Every child, of every ability, bears full dignity; we counsel accordingly.
closing: May every learner be seen whole, and may your understanding open every door they need.
